build_stamp.note: Canonical data file — single source of truth. Edit this; then re-run the renderer to regenerate SPEC_DIMENSIONAL_MAP.md.

scope_note: Spine + calibration only. Covers the 7 algebraic-spine theorems, 4 dimensionless physical identifications, the 3 calibration declarations theorem-enforced by FTD-0059 + FTD-0096, and 1 worked dimensional application (m_e in MeV). Full SM-quantity coverage lives in CATALOG_PARAMETRIC_INSERTIONS.md.

epistemic_legend.THEOREM: Rigorously proven from axioms; inputs and proof trace are explicit
epistemic_legend.STRONGLY MOTIVATED CONJECTURE: Polynomial-level theorem with strong empirical match; physical identification not uniquely forced
epistemic_legend.CALIBRATION: Declared (not derived) anchor; theorem-enforced as the irreducible minimum by no-go results (FTD-0059, FTD-0096)
epistemic_legend.IMPOSED: Parametric anchor that fixes a unit; same epistemic status as CALIBRATION but assigned to a specific FTD constant

entries.label: G* algebraic identity
entries.notes: Direct Chowla–Selberg evaluation of L(s, χ_{-4}) at s=1 on the lemniscatic curve y² = x³ − x. Four independent derivations enumerated in MONOGRAPH_GSTAR_BRIDGE_CONSTANT (Γ-ratio, Watson period integral, lemniscate arc length, modular-form value).

entries.label: Master quadratic polynomial + roots
entries.notes: Two independent derivations (FTD-0081): Route A (physics — Gaussian J-integration of S_E) and Route B (arithmetic — Damerell–Shimura at CM curve E_i). Both produce the identical polynomial to 100 digits.

entries.label: CM curve uniqueness among class-number-1 fields
entries.ftd_formula: Among d ∈ {-3, -4, -7, -8, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}, only d = -4 yields master-quadratic roots that simultaneously match dimensionless physical constants to permille precision
entries.notes: Numerical verification across all 9 class-number-1 discriminants. Uniqueness extends only within the class-number-1 family; class-number ≥ 2 is [OPEN].

entries.label: Coefficient 16 = |Aut(E)|²
entries.ftd_formula: For E: y² = x³ − x, |Aut(E)| = 4 over ℚ̄, so |Aut(E)|² = 16 (the master-quadratic coefficient)
entries.notes: Three independent routes converge on 16: direct |Aut(E)|² (Route A, FTD-0006); z_BCC × 2 (Route B, FTD-0007); j-invariant + modular form (additional).

entries.label: Watson identity W₃ = G*²/(2π)
entries.ftd_formula: W₃ := ∫_0^π dx ∫_0^π dy ∫_0^π dz [3 − cos x − cos y − cos z]⁻¹ / π³ = G*²/(2π)
entries.notes: Watson's third triple integral. Bundled with G* under FTD-0002 because it is one of the four independent derivations of G*; here it is also recorded as a structural identity in its own right (the BCC eigenvalue triple-cosine product).

entries.label: Phase G geometric Coulomb identity
entries.ftd_formula: α_r(r, L) = 2·r·G_L(r), where G_L is the periodic lattice Poisson Green's function. Holds at every finite L without free parameters.

lab_measurement.value_note: R² = 1.0000 at L=384, median 0.07% residual in the Coulomb tail

entries.notes: Reframed away from the QED-deviation reading: the lattice α plateau at ≈1.8× α_ref is the Poisson Green's function shape, not a fine-structure correction. Zero free parameters.

entries.label: Phase J partition-function ultralocality at L=2
entries.ftd_formula: At L=2, the partition function Z factorizes site-locally: Z = ∏_v Z_v(s_v, J_v). No connected correlators between voxels.
entries.notes: Direct algebraic statement about the L=2 partition function. Empirical engine support: FTD-0075 (flux propagator on Langevin ensemble shows essentially constant correlator at distance, consistent with ultralocality).

entries.label: 1/α (fine-structure constant) ↔ master-quadratic root x₊
entries.ftd_formula: x₊ root of master quadratic; tree value 137.0362, with 7-term 1-loop series matching CODATA to 24 digits (post-hoc fit beyond CODATA precision per AUDIT_MASTER_QUADRATIC)

comparison.method: tree x₊ vs CODATA: 1.26 ppm; full 7-term 1-loop series matches CODATA to within published precision

entries.notes: Polynomial-level theorem (x₊ is a root of a number-theoretic polynomial); the physical identification x₊ = 1/α is [STRONGLY MOTIVATED CONJECTURE] (downgraded from THEOREM 2026-04-19) because it depends on dual-match + CM-curve uniqueness rather than a derivation chain to QED. FTD-0097 look-elsewhere scan (2026-04-27) confirms the master quadratic's polynomial-root layer lives outside the monomial scan space and is unaffected by the over-richness verdict.

entries.label: N_c (number of colors) ↔ master-quadratic root x₋
entries.ftd_formula: x₋ root of master quadratic; numerical value 3.024

lab_measurement.source: Standard Model (exact integer, not a measurement)

comparison.method: x₋ = 3.024 vs N_c = 3 exactly (0.80% off integer)

entries.notes: Same epistemic tier as α: polynomial-root layer is theorem; physical identification is conjecture. Four independent topological routes converge on N_c = 3 (DERIV_NC_FROM_TOPOLOGY).

entries.label: m_μ / m_e (muon/electron mass ratio)
entries.notes: Derived from framework integers {b₃=7, N_c=3} with no free parameters. The formula is integer arithmetic; the 0.11% gap to CODATA is the radiative correction not yet computed in FTD.

entries.label: m_τ / m_e (tau/electron mass ratio)
entries.notes: Derived from framework integers {N_eff=13, N_base=4, N_c=3, b₃=7} with no free parameters. 0.01% match to PDG.

entries.label: a_phys ≡ ℓ_P (length anchor)
entries.calibration_note: FTD-0059 (no-go theorem, 2026-04-23): no length is expressible from Axiom-Zero invariants alone. Mechanisms α/β/γ/δ all closed negative. The Planck-length declaration is theorem-enforced as the irreducible minimum, not a convenience choice. ℓ_P value from CODATA 2022: ≈1.616255 × 10⁻³⁵ m.
entries.notes: First of two SI-dimensional calibrations theorem-enforced by FTD-0096.

entries.label: t_phys (one tick in seconds)
entries.ftd_formula: t_phys = √3 · ℓ_P / c (CFL condition c_lat = 1/√3 + a_phys ≡ ℓ_P + c_phys = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s)
entries.calibration_note: Derived (not declared) from a_phys ≡ ℓ_P and the CFL stability constraint c_lat = 1/√3 (which is itself a [THEOREM] from the cubic-lattice wave equation). Numerically t_phys ≈ 9.34 × 10⁻⁴⁴ s.
entries.notes: Once a_phys is fixed, t_phys is fully determined. No additional calibration freedom.

entries.label: K_B = m_e (mass-unit anchor)
entries.ftd_formula: DECLARED: lattice manifestation threshold K_B = 0.511 in lattice units corresponds to m_e in physical units. Mass-unit ≡ m_e/K_B = 1 MeV/c².

comparison.method: K_B parametrically anchored to m_e by definition; the comparison is to confirm the calibration is consistently applied in scripts/constants.py (K_B = 0.511 to 3 sig figs)

entries.calibration_note: FTD-0096 (calibration-interface theorem, 2026-04-28): mass-unit μ_FTD is calibration, not derivation, on equal footing with a_phys. Three independent closures of FTD-0094 confirm this from methodological (FTD-0097 look-elsewhere null-rejected upward), structural-mechanism (FTD-0093 Mechanism C closed negative), and dimensional (this no-go) sides. Exactly two SI-dimensional calibrations (a_phys ≡ ℓ_P and K_B = m_e) are theorem-enforced as the irreducible minimum.
entries.notes: Second of two SI-dimensional calibrations. Together with a_phys, completes the calibration interface.

entries.label: m_e (electron mass in MeV/c²) — worked example
entries.ftd_formula: m_e = K_B (lattice value 0.511) × mass-unit (1 MeV/c² per K_B unit) = 0.511 MeV/c²

comparison.method: 0.511 (K_B, 3 sig figs) vs 0.51099895069 (CODATA): bookkeeping match by definition of the anchor. The +2053 ppb gap is purely the precision of K_B as stored in scripts/constants.py — not a physical disagreement.

entries.calibration_note: This is the bridge mechanism: every dimensional FTD prediction reduces to (a) a dimensionless ratio (e.g. m_μ/m_e = 207) times (b) the mass-unit anchor (1 MeV/c² ≡ m_e/K_B). The same pattern applies to lengths (multiply dimensionless ratio by a_phys = ℓ_P) and times (multiply by t_phys = √3·ℓ_P/c).
entries.notes: Single worked example. Other dimensional consequences (m_μ in MeV via 207 × m_e, m_p in MeV via m_p/m_e × m_e, etc.) follow the same pattern and are catalogued individually in CATALOG_PARAMETRIC_INSERTIONS.md.
